title: Diversity contraction: boundary law, Mediation Ratchet and The Bead Count
description: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates (#779, June 2026) claims a boundary law for semantic exhaustion with three cases and states its falsifiers through type-resolution tests, the elasticity ρ of the Mediation Ratchet and the rate of off-distribution production; the archive's holographic compression (#863, later in June) restates the Ratchet's falsifier for source diversity across summarization cycles. The Bead Count (#782) registers numeric forecasts against it, such as case-3 classification at fine resolution, cross-domain ρ above 0.5 and a critical real-data mixing fraction between 0.05 and 0.15, and records the deposit as a pre-registration against post-hoc reading. Constitutive Mediation (#781) claims that cohorts formed under heavy mediation will show suppressed cross-context propagation and states its falsifier; #1540 names the components on which the boundary law's transposition fails. The page also holds unrelated claims from The Final Time (#1635, #1637).

claims.statement: The Ratchet is disconfirmed if a substrate with scarcity-responsive mediation ($\rho > \rho^*$) and a measured human floor does not develop a low-diversity trap. Conversely, if mediation under realistic adoption *preserves* fine-grained diversity across corpora, without explicit diversity-injection design, over a multi-year window, the Ratchet is not engaging under real-world conditions. That is a genuine possibility the framework must accommodate; a theory that treats every preservation as hidden suppression is not falsifiable.

The Diversity Contraction / Mediation Ratchet describes the progressive narrowing of source diversity in AI-mediated knowledge: each summarization cycle reduces the number of distinct sources contributing to the synthesized output, approaching a threshold α* = p/g₀ beyond which minority positions are structurally excluded regardless of their validity; this is falsified if empirical measurement shows source diversity increasing through successive AI summarization cycles.
